title: How can the primes of 225 list all its factors?
description: The primes of two hundred and twenty five are multiplied one at a time, two at a time, three at a time and all together, then one is added. Together these give all nine factors of the number. Keeko's doubt, that only the primes are factors, is tested with nine.
teaching_notes: One idea: every subpart of the prime factorisation, multiplied, gives a factor, and adding one completes the list. Watch for students who list only the primes themselves.

source: List all the factors of 225 using its prime factorisation.
video_script.why: The child can factorise into primes but has not yet built every factor from the primes in an organised way.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the primes one at a time, two at a time, three at a time and all together, then add one.
video_script.anchor: The number two hundred and twenty five written as its four primes, five, five, three and three.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the factors are only the primes, three and five. But nine divides two hundred and twenty five too, and nine is not prime.
video_script.payoff_line: Two hundred and twenty five has nine factors.

final_answer.spoken: one, three, five, nine, fifteen, twenty five, forty five, seventy five and two hundred and twenty five

maths_rules: One prime at a time: 3 and 5.
Three primes: 3 x 3 x 5 = 45, 3 x 5 x 5 = 75.
All four: 3 x 3 x 5 x 5 = 225. And the factor 1.
Slip: 9 divides 225 (225 / 9 = 25) and 9 is not prime.
video_script.design: One idea: every subpart of the primes gives a factor, taken in order of size of the subpart. Assumes prime factorisation. Wrong idea: the factors are only the primes. The four primes stay on the board all video.
